decisions.reason: As a peripheral consumer product with only limited visibility and weaker fit to the firm's industrial waste-to-energy capabilities, it is the most likely to fall below aspiration levels and be cut so resources can be redirected to higher-priority ventures.

These modular plant extensions fit the firm's established engineering business and allow incremental adaptation across models, so with industry growth and some organizational slack management would likely keep them on the market.
Because this waste-oil-to-energy plant is both tightly aligned with the core offer and presented as a flagship, management would be inclined to tolerate early uncertainty and continue supporting it.

Although commercially and technically more uncertain than some core offerings, its strategic fit with the firm's circular-fuel direction and flagship status make continued retention more likely than withdrawal.
